subject: Telescope post-demo: model evaluation plan & acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Moreno <ava.moreno@telescope.ai>, Kai Liu <kai.liu@telescope.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: initial benchmark plan and next steps

Hi Ava / Kai,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — appreciate the clear walkthrough of the query patterns and the two high-volume endpoints (inference: search-summarize; assist: multi-turn QA). Suggested next steps from our side so we can set up a focused eval run: 

1) Redwood runs a 3-model comparison on your representative prompt bundle (attached prompt-set-v1.jsonl):
   - Open candidate: Llama-3-13B-QLoRA (optimized with Redwood quant config)
   - RedTeam / Redwood curated: Redwood-Atlas-7B-opt (fast path, lower mem)
   - Customer baseline: InternalLarge v1 (your proprietary baseline provided in logs)

2) Evaluation metrics we'll produce: token-level latency (p50/p95), cost per 1k tokens, domain F1 (QA), top-line hallucination rate (measured by hallucination-check suite), and end-to-end throughput under 120ms SLO target.

3) Acceptance thresholds proposal (we can adjust once we see your initial logs):
   - Domain F1 >= 0.78 compared to baseline
   - Hallucination rate <= 3% absolute (measured on your test prompts)
   - p95 latency < 180ms on a single dedicated GPU instance
   - Token cost <= 0.85x baseline (goal: reduce unit cost while matching quality)

If those acceptance thresholds look reasonable, we'll kick off a 10-day sandbox trial (isolated, dedicated capacity) and share a CSV of per-prompt outputs + a short readout. I've attached the prompt bundle and will follow up with a short statement of work (SOW) that covers trial scope.

Could you confirm: 1) a contact for granting sandbox/data access; 2) the baseline model artifacts (if you can share weights or an RPC endpoint) or logs if not; 3) any disallowed behaviors/guardrails to include in the eval (sensitive entities, PII rules, safety blockers)?

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: prompt-set-v1.jsonl (19 prompts)
From: Ava Moreno <ava.moreno@telescope.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Kai Liu <kai.liu@telescope.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: initial benchmark plan and next steps

Thanks Ben — this is helpful.

We can grant sandbox access once your SOW is signed. Procurement looped in (procurement@telescope.ai) for the SOW. Quick answers:
- Baseline: we can provide logs and a lightweight RPC endpoint for InternalLarge v1 (no weights). I attached a small anonymized sample trace (telescope-benchmark-results.csv) in this reply.
- Guardrails: please strip/gap anonymized PII if you return full-text outputs; we prefer a 60-day retention window during the trial.

Acceptance thresholds look directionally fair, but our leadership asked for an additional regression check on structured field extraction (we use the model to pull address, company-name, and invoice-id from messy input). Can you include a per-field precision/recall metric for the trial?

Also, can you clarify how you'll measure hallucination rate? We saw a few hallucinated entities in the demo and want the definition to be explicit.

Appreciate it — Ava
Product Lead, Telescope AI

---
Attachment: telescope-benchmark-results.csv (sample, 200 rows)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: initial benchmark plan and next steps (internal)

Ben / Priyom — quick internal note to refine the evaluation matrix before we send the SOW back to Ava: 

1) Definitions and measurement approach (important so client and legal agree):
   - Hallucination: any factual string in the model output that is not supported by the input or by a provided ground-truth doc set. We'll mark entity-level hallucination separately for extraction tasks.
   - Entity extraction metrics: calculate per-field precision/recall/F1 (address, company-name, invoice-id) on the client's labeled subset. If they lack labels, run a human review on a stratified sample (50 examples).

2) Additional acceptance gates (recommended):
   - No single-category regression > 5% F1 drop vs baseline on any critical extraction field.
   - Average human-review time for error triage should not exceed 120s per flagged example (ops cost proxy).

3) Model shortlist and why:
   - Llama-3-13B-QLoRA (open): strong recall on noisy prompts after light fine-tuning; cost-efficient with 8-bit compression.
   - Redwood-Atlas-7B-opt (curated open): better latency profile and stable generative constraints; likely to meet p95 targets.
   - InternalLarge v1 (customer baseline): compare for quality regressions and edge-case hallucination.

4) Deliverables for SOW: trial window (10 business days), evaluation CSV, per-prompt diff against baseline, readout deck, and a small regression-alert rulebook (if an output pattern shows >3% hallucination spikes).

I'll draft the SOW language for the trial scope and attach a short appendix for measurement definitions before Ben sends to Ava. Priyom: can you confirm we have the human-review pool capacity (QA reviewers) for up to 150 labeled checks during the trial?

-Neha
Director, Customer Solutions
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Moreno <ava.moreno@telescope.ai>
Cc: Kai Liu <kai.liu@telescope.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, procurement@telescope.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: initial benchmark plan and next steps

Hi Ava / Kai,

Thanks for the sample trace and for the point on extraction metrics — good call. Attached: 1) short SOW (trial-sow.docx) that mirrors Neha's deliverables list, 2) the prompt bundle you already saw, and 3) a CSV template we'll populate with the per-prompt diffs.

Clarifying the hallucination measurement (as Neha summarized):
- We run an automated entity-match step for extraction tasks (exact / fuzzy matching rules) and flag mismatches as potential hallucinations.
- Human review on a stratified 50–150 sample will confirm whether flagged mismatches are true hallucinations.
- Hallucination rate in our report = confirmed hallucinations / total evaluated outputs. We'll show both automated-flag rate and human-confirmed rate so you can see false positives from the heuristics.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: Ben sends SOW for signature and request sandbox invite.
- Once SOW signed (procurement): Redwood provisions a dedicated sandbox and kicks off a 10-business-day run.
- Day 3 readout: early metrics and any immediate regressions.
- Final readout: per-field extraction F1, hallucination confirmed rate, latency/cost breakdown, and model recommendation.

If this looks good, please: 1) confirm the procurement next-step (signer + expected turnaround), and 2) share the sandbox contact (ssh/API endpoint owner + creds flow).

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: trial-sow.docx (SOW, 2 pages), prompt-set-v1.jsonl (19 prompts), CSV template: telemetry-diff-template.csv
